cases.refreshed: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEaM adventure every week. Active engagement with STEaM promotes academic success. The topic list is subject to change; please check back or call the branch for up-to-date details. Suggested ages vary; please refer to individual program descriptions. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Aug 18 - The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing & Pepper Experiment. Participants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap. Aug 25 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been rescheduled for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly. Sept 1 - Marble Run Fun. Harness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run. Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (please note topic change). In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up. Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time). Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients. Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest. Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch. Sept 22 - Mental Math: Multiplication. Children have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition. Oct 6 - Wind Turbine Engineering. In this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Oct 13 - Paper Rockets. Learn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest! Participants will learn about propulsion, then create their own rockets. Oct 20 - Properties of Water (Science from Scientists). Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion and surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique properties of water. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program. Oct 27 - TBA; Nov 3 - Learn About Aerodynamics Through Paper Planes. In this high-flying workshop, participants will build different types of paper planes and learn concepts of aerodynamics and the impact of plane design through fun and interactive experiments. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Nov 10 - Ozobot Maze Runner. Teach your Ozobot to navigate a maze using simple color codes. Nov 17 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Nov 24 - TBA; Dec 1 - Let's Build Parachutes. In this workshop, participants will build parachutes of different shapes, sizes and materials, and observe the impact of their design. They will participate in fun parachute drops with different loads while learning the science behind parachute design. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Dec 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge. In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.

events.title: Books & Bricks Book Club for Grades 4-6

cases.refreshed: Join our book and LEGO building club for fourth to sixth graders! This month we are reading the graphic novel Duel by Jessixa Bagley. We will meet on Monday, November 16th at 3:30 PM in the Program Room. Please read the book before our meeting. At the meeting we will discuss the book and do a LEGO building activity. Special thanks to the Friends of Milpitas Library for making this program possible. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
